requirements.title: Adversarial flags and their validation
requirements.rationale: A review that is off by default leaves every existing run unchanged, and a malformed round count is refused before any money is spent.

criteria.action: register a boolean flag `--adversarial` that is off by default and an integer flag `--adversarial-rounds`, and use a round limit of 1 when `--adversarial` is on and `--adversarial-rounds` is not given
criteria.contract: adversarial is false when not given; adversarial is true and the resulting Options round limit is 1 with `--adversarial` alone; the round limit is 3 when `--adversarial-rounds 3` is given

setup: the spec command's flag set
check.pseudocode: o = specOptions(parse([])); assert !o.Adversarial; o = specOptions(parse(['--adversarial'])); assert o.Adversarial && o.AdversarialRounds == 1; o = specOptions(parse(['--adversarial','--adversarial-rounds','3'])); assert o.AdversarialRounds == 3

criteria.condition: `--adversarial-rounds` is given with a value below 1 or above 5, including an explicit `0`, with or without `--preflight`
criteria.action: reject the invocation as a usage error before any input is fetched or any model is called
criteria.contract: exit code 2, error category `usage`, no phase recorded in usage and no file written

setup: a stub provider and a fetch hook that fail the test if called
an empty specs dir
check.pseudocode: for n in [0,6,-1]: for pf in [false,true]: r = runSpec(args(n, pf)); assert r.exit == 2; assert r.env.error.category == 'usage'; assert fetchCalls == 0 && modelCalls == 0; assert len(r.env.usage.phases) == 0; assert dirEmpty(specsDir)

criteria.condition: `--adversarial-rounds` is given while `--adversarial` is off, with or without `--preflight`
criteria.action: reject the invocation as a usage error before any input is fetched or any model is called
criteria.contract: exit code 2, error category `usage`, no phase recorded in usage and no file written

setup: a stub provider and a fetch hook that fail the test if called
check.pseudocode: for pf in [false,true]: r = runSpec(['--adversarial-rounds','2'] + pf); assert r.exit == 2 && r.env.error.category == 'usage'; assert modelCalls == 0 && fetchCalls == 0

criteria.condition: `--adversarial-rounds` is given a value that is not an integer
criteria.action: reject the invocation through the flag parser before any input is fetched or any model is called
criteria.contract: exit code 2, error category `usage`

setup: a stub provider that fails the test if called
check.pseudocode: for v in ['abc','1.5']: r = runSpec(['--adversarial','--adversarial-rounds',v]); assert r.exit == 2; assert r.env.error.category == 'usage'; assert modelCalls == 0

criteria.condition: `--adversarial` is off
criteria.action: run the same phases with the same prompts, and produce the same result, summary sentence, files on disk and `usage.phases[]` entries as a run of the same input before this feature, with no `review` field in any package
criteria.contract: the phases run are exactly prd, requirements, test_spec and tasks; no package carries a `review` field in the JSON result; the summary sentence has no `review:` clause; the package directory holds only the files the format defines; usage.phases[] names are exactly prd, requirements, test_spec, tasks

setup: the real specgen pipeline over the valid_spec fixture with a scripted author and a reviewer fake that fails the test if called
Adversarial is off
check.pseudocode: res = Run(ctx, opts{Adversarial:false}); assert phaseNames(res) == ['prd','requirements','test_spec','tasks']; assert reviewerCalls == 0; assert !contains(json(res), '"review"'); assert !contains(res.Summary(), 'review:')

criteria.condition: `--dry-run` is given together with `--adversarial`
criteria.action: run the review and revision phases as in a real run, write no file, and report each package's `review` with the same fields and values a real run would report
criteria.contract: the dry run invoked prd_review and prd_revision; the dry run wrote no file; the dry run's package review equals the real run's package review field by field

setup: the real pipeline with scripted author, reviewer and reviser returning a major finding then no findings
two runs of the same input: one with --dry-run, one real
check.pseudocode: d = Run(opts{DryRun:true, Adversarial:true, Rounds:2}); r = Run(opts{Adversarial:true, Rounds:2}); assert noFiles(dryDir); assert d.Package.Review == r.Package.Review

requirements.title: The review phase
requirements.rationale: A reviewer that did not write the PRD and sees everything the author saw can find flaws the author's blind spots hid.

criteria.condition: a review phase starts
criteria.action: start a fresh conversation that is sent the current PRD (spec name, title, body, open questions and `relevant_files`), the original input, any `--context`, the current `codebase_notes` labelled as the author's claims to be checked against the code and not as facts, the language block, the steering, the repository map, the landscape of existing specs, and the read-only file tools plus `code_search` when the index exists
criteria.contract: the phase Kind is prd_review and its name is `prd_review`; the prompt contains the spec name, title, body, an open question and a relevant file of the PRD; the prompt contains the original input and the --context text; the notes appear labelled as the author's claims to be checked against the code, not as facts; the system prompt carries the language block, steering, repository map and landscape of existing specs; the built-in tools are the read-only file tools, plus code_search when the index exists; the prompt is not a continuation of the PRD phase's conversation

setup: a recording runner that captures the agentrun.Phase of every call
a PRD with open questions, relevant files and codebase_notes 'NOTE-X', input text and `--context` text
check.pseudocode: ph = recorder.last(); assert ph.Kind == 'prd_review'; assert contains(ph.User, prd.Body) && contains(ph.User, 'NOTE-X'); assert contains(ph.User, 'claims') && contains(ph.User, 'not facts'); assert ph.BuiltinTools == WithCodeSearch(ReadOnlyFileTools, cs); assert ph.History == nil

criteria.condition: a review phase starts and the PRD is one scope of a split
criteria.action: also send every scope's name and one-line scope, which scope this PRD covers, what the earlier scopes deliver as the PRD phase was shown it, and the statement that work belonging to another scope is not a dropped ask, without the PRD-writing instructions the PRD phase receives
criteria.contract: the prompt lists every scope's name and one-line scope; the prompt says which scope this PRD covers; the prompt carries what scope 1 delivered as the PRD phase was shown it; the prompt states that work belonging to another scope is not a dropped ask; the prompt does not contain the PRD-writing instructions of the split block

setup: a three-scope split plan where scope 2 is under review and scope 1 has a draft PRD and notes
check.pseudocode: p = reviewPrompt(prd2, splitCtx(plan, 1, drafts, notes)); for s in plan: assert contains(p, s.Name) && contains(p, s.Scope); assert contains(p, 'not a dropped ask'); assert !contains(p, writeInstructionsText)

criteria.action: instruct the reviewer to find flaws rather than approve, and to look for behaviours without an error path, goals that cannot be verified, claims in the PRD or notes that the code contradicts, a proposed component that already exists under another name, scope the input did not ask for, asks of the input the PRD dropped, wording two readers would turn into different requirements, sections that contradict each other, Design Decisions whose reason does not hold, and internal design (package layout, types, signatures) that leaked into the PRD
criteria.contract: the review phase's system prompt names each of the listed flaw kinds and tells the reviewer not to approve the PRD

setup: the review system prompt
check.pseudocode: s = prdReviewSystemPrompt(); for k in flawKindKeywords: assert contains(lower(s), k); assert contains(lower(s), 'not approve') or contains(lower(s), 'do not approve')

criteria.action: end the review through a submit tool that takes a list of findings, possibly empty, in which each finding carries a severity from `critical`, `major` or `minor`, a section, a flaw, an evidence, a remedy and a `reopens` id that may be empty
criteria.contract: both are accepted and terminate the phase; the schema requires severity (enum critical, major, minor), section, flaw, evidence, remedy and reopens in each finding; the sink holds the submitted findings

setup: a review tool bound to a sink for round 1
check.pseudocode: r = tool.Execute(json({findings:[]})); assert r.Terminate && sink.get() == []; r = tool.Execute(json({findings:[f]})); assert r.Terminate; assert schema.item.required == ['severity','section','flaw','evidence','remedy','reopens']

criteria.condition: the review tool accepts a submission in round r
criteria.action: assign each submitted finding the id `R<r>-F<n>`, with n counting from 1 in the order the findings were submitted
criteria.contract: ids such as `R2-F3` that are unique within the PRD's review and unchanged for the rest of the run

setup: a review tool for round 2 with no earlier findings that are reopened
check.pseudocode: tool = newReviewTool(round=2, earlier=[]); tool.Execute(three); assert ids(sink.get()) == ['R2-F1','R2-F2','R2-F3']

criteria.condition: the reviewer ends its conversation without an accepted submission
criteria.action: report the phase as not finished, so that the round loop handles it as a review failure
criteria.contract: a no-result error for phase `prd_review` naming the review tool

setup: a runner fake that finishes the review conversation without calling the submit tool
check.pseudocode: _, _, err = reviewer.Review(ctx, req); assert err != nil; assert contains(err.Error(), 'prd_review') && contains(err.Error(), ToolSubmitPRDReview)

requirements.title: Review submission checks
requirements.rationale: A finding without evidence or a verbatim repeat of a rejected finding costs a revision without giving it anything to check.

criteria.condition: a review submission contains more than 30 findings
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviewer, record no finding from it, and keep the phase running
criteria.contract: a tool error that names the finding count and the limit of 30

setup: a review tool in round 1
check.pseudocode: r = tool.Execute(n(31)); assert r.IsError && contains(r.Msg,'31') && contains(r.Msg,'30'); assert !r.Terminate && sink.empty(); r = tool.Execute(n(30)); assert r.Terminate

criteria.condition: a finding in a review submission has an empty severity, section, flaw, evidence or remedy
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviewer, record no finding from it, and tell it to support or withdraw each such finding
criteria.contract: a tool error that names each offending finding by its position and its empty fields

setup: a review tool in round 1
check.pseudocode: r = tool.Execute([ok, noEvidence, noSevNoRemedy]); assert r.IsError; assert contains(r.Msg,'2') && contains(r.Msg,'evidence') && contains(r.Msg,'severity') && contains(r.Msg,'remedy'); assert sink.empty()

criteria.condition: a finding in a round-1 review submission has a non-empty `reopens`
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviewer and record no finding from it
criteria.contract: a tool error that names each offending finding

setup: a review tool in round 1
check.pseudocode: r = tool.Execute([f{reopens:'R1-F1'}]); assert r.IsError && contains(r.Msg,'1'); assert sink.empty()

criteria.condition: a finding in a later round's review submission has a `reopens` that names no earlier finding of this PRD
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviewer and record no finding from it
criteria.contract: a tool error that names each offending finding and the unknown id

setup: a review tool in round 2 with earlier findings R1-F1 and R1-F2
check.pseudocode: r = tool2.Execute([f{reopens:'R1-F9'}]); assert r.IsError && contains(r.Msg,'R1-F9'); assert sink.empty()

criteria.condition: a finding in a later round's review submission reopens an earlier `rejected` finding with evidence identical to that finding's evidence after whitespace normalisation
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviewer and record no finding from it
criteria.contract: a tool error that names each offending finding and the rejected finding it repeats

setup: a round-2 review tool whose earlier R1-F1 is rejected with evidence 'a  b\nc'
check.pseudocode: r = tool2.Execute([f{reopens:'R1-F1', evidence:' a b c '}]); assert r.IsError && contains(r.Msg,'R1-F1'); r = tool2.Execute([f{reopens:'R1-F1', evidence:'new'}]); assert r.Terminate

criteria.condition: a finding in a later round's review submission has an empty `reopens` and the same section text and flaw text as an earlier `rejected` finding
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviewer and record no finding from it
criteria.contract: a tool error that names each offending finding and the rejected finding it repeats

setup: a round-2 review tool whose earlier R1-F1 is rejected with section 'Goals' and flaw 'X is untestable'
check.pseudocode: r = tool2.Execute([f{reopens:'',section:'Goals',flaw:'X is untestable'}]); assert r.IsError && contains(r.Msg,'R1-F1'); assert sink.empty()

criteria.action: for any two evidence strings that differ only in leading or trailing whitespace or in the length or kind of internal whitespace runs, treat them as identical, and for any two that differ in a non-whitespace character, treat them as different
criteria.contract: normalised equality holds for the whitespace-only variants; normalised equality does not hold when a non-whitespace character differs

setup: the evidence normalisation function used for the repeat check
check.pseudocode: for a in gen_strings(): b = perturbWhitespace(a); assert sameEvidence(a,b); c = mutateNonSpaceChar(a); assert !sameEvidence(a,c)

requirements.title: The revision phase
requirements.rationale: A third agent weighs each finding on its evidence instead of defending the author's choices, and cannot change what the split depends on.

criteria.condition: a review raised at least one finding and its revision phase starts
criteria.action: start a fresh conversation, separate from the PRD phase and the review, that is sent the current PRD, the round's findings with their ids, the original input, any `--context`, the current `codebase_notes`, and the same split context, run context and read-only tools as the review
criteria.contract: the phase Kind is prd_revision with a fresh conversation; the prompt carries the PRD, R1-F1 and R1-F2 with their fields, the input, the --context and the notes; the split context, language block, steering, repository map, landscape and read-only tools equal those of the review phase

setup: a recording runner and a round-1 review that returned findings R1-F1 and R1-F2
a split scope PRD
check.pseudocode: rev = recorder.byKind('prd_revision'); rv = recorder.byKind('prd_review'); assert contains(rev.User,'R1-F1') && contains(rev.User,input); assert rev.BuiltinTools == rv.BuiltinTools; assert splitBlockOf(rev) == splitBlockOf(rv); assert rev.History == nil

criteria.action: instruct the reviser to answer every finding as `accepted`, changing the PRD to remedy it, or as `rejected` with a reason that says why the finding does not hold, and to record in `## Design Decisions` what each accepted remedy settled
criteria.contract: it tells the reviser to answer every finding as accepted or rejected; it requires a rejected reason that says why the finding does not hold, not merely disagreement; it tells the reviser to record what each accepted remedy settled in `## Design Decisions`

setup: the revision system prompt
check.pseudocode: s = prdRevisionSystemPrompt(); assert contains(s,'accepted') && contains(s,'rejected') && contains(s,'## Design Decisions') && contains(s,'does not hold')

criteria.action: require the complete revised body and the dispositions, accept optional replacement `open_questions`, `relevant_files` and `codebase_notes`, and offer no field for the spec name, the title or the split
criteria.contract: body and dispositions are required; open_questions, relevant_files and codebase_notes are optional; there is no spec_name, title or recommended_split property

setup: the revision tool's input schema
check.pseudocode: s = revisionSchema(); assert required(s) == ['body','dispositions']; assert optional(s) == ['open_questions','relevant_files','codebase_notes']; assert !has(s,'spec_name') && !has(s,'title') && !has(s,'recommended_split')

criteria.condition: the revision tool accepts a submission
criteria.action: produce a revised PRD that carries the submitted body and the spec name, title and recommended split of the PRD it revises
criteria.contract: the revised PRD's spec name, title and recommended split equal those of the PRD under revision

setup: a PRD with spec name 'widget_cache', title 'Widget cache' and a recommended split of two scopes
check.pseudocode: out = sink.get(); assert out.Body == newBody; assert out.SpecName == prd.SpecName && out.Title == prd.Title && out.RecommendedSplit == prd.RecommendedSplit

criteria.condition: the revision tool accepts a submission
criteria.action: keep the earlier value of each optional field that is omitted, replace it with each supplied value, clear `open_questions` or `relevant_files` when an empty list is supplied, and keep the earlier notes when an empty `codebase_notes` is supplied
criteria.contract: omitted fields keep the earlier values; supplied fields replace the earlier values; empty open_questions and relevant_files lists clear them; empty codebase_notes keeps 'OLD'

setup: a PRD with two open questions, two relevant files and notes 'OLD'
check.pseudocode: a = apply(omitAll); assert a.OpenQuestions == prd.OpenQuestions && a.CodebaseNotes == 'OLD'; b = apply({open_questions:[]}); assert len(b.OpenQuestions) == 0; c = apply({codebase_notes:''}); assert c.CodebaseNotes == 'OLD'

criteria.condition: the replacement `codebase_notes` of an accepted revision exceed 12000 bytes
criteria.action: bound the notes to 12000 bytes by the same rule the PRD phase applies to its notes
criteria.contract: the revised PRD's notes are at most 12000 bytes long

setup: a revision submission with codebase_notes of 20000 bytes
check.pseudocode: out = sink.get(); assert len(out.CodebaseNotes) <= 12000; assert out.CodebaseNotes == boundNotes(big)

criteria.condition: the reviser ends its conversation without an accepted submission
criteria.action: report the phase as not finished, so that the round loop handles it as a revision failure
criteria.contract: a no-result error for phase `prd_revision` naming the revision tool

setup: a runner fake that finishes without calling the revision submit tool
check.pseudocode: _, _, err = reviser.Revise(ctx, req); assert contains(err.Error(),'prd_revision') && contains(err.Error(), ToolSubmitPRDRevision)

requirements.title: Revision submission checks
requirements.rationale: Every finding must get exactly one answer, an acceptance must change the PRD, and a revised PRD must pass the checks the PRD phase applies.

criteria.condition: a revision submission leaves a finding of this round without a disposition, gives a finding two dispositions, or has a disposition naming an id that is not one of this round's findings
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviser and record nothing from it
criteria.contract: a tool error that names each missing, duplicated or unknown finding id

setup: a revision tool for findings R1-F1, R1-F2 and R1-F3
check.pseudocode: r = tool.Execute(dispositions([F1,F1,F2,F9])); assert r.IsError; assert contains(r.Msg,'R1-F1') && contains(r.Msg,'R1-F3') && contains(r.Msg,'R1-F9'); assert sink.empty()

criteria.condition: a `rejected` disposition in a revision submission has an empty reason
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviser and record nothing from it
criteria.contract: a tool error that names each finding id whose rejection has no reason

setup: a revision tool for findings R1-F1 and R1-F2
check.pseudocode: r = tool.Execute([acc(F1), rej(F2,'  ')]); assert r.IsError && contains(r.Msg,'R1-F2'); assert sink.empty()

criteria.condition: a revision submission accepts at least one finding and its body, `open_questions`, `relevant_files` and notes, after the keep-or-replace rule, are all identical to those of the PRD under revision
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviser and record nothing from it
criteria.contract: a tool error that says the accepted findings left the PRD unchanged

setup: a revision tool for one finding
check.pseudocode: r = tool.Execute(accept + sameBody); assert r.IsError && contains(r.Msg,'unchanged'); assert sink.empty(); r = tool.Execute(reject + sameBody); assert r.Terminate

criteria.condition: the revised body has no `## Intent` section by afspec's rule, or starts with YAML frontmatter
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviser with the same rejection the PRD phase gives for the same body
criteria.contract: a tool error with the PRD phase's code for the failed check

setup: the PRD tool's rejection codes for the same bodies
check.pseudocode: for body in [noIntent, withFrontmatter]: assert revTool.Execute(body).Code == prdTool.Execute(prdWith(body)).Code

criteria.condition: a path supplied in `relevant_files` is not a regular file in the workspace
criteria.action: turn the submission back to the reviser and record nothing from it
criteria.contract: a tool error that names each offending path

setup: a workspace containing file a.go and a directory d/
check.pseudocode: r = tool.Execute(files(['missing.go','d'])); assert r.IsError && contains(r.Msg,'missing.go') && contains(r.Msg,'d'); assert sink.empty()

criteria.condition: a revision submission changes the text of `## Intent` and passes every other check
criteria.action: accept the submission
criteria.contract: the revised PRD carries the changed `## Intent` text

setup: a revision tool and a PRD whose Intent says 'old intent'
check.pseudocode: r = tool.Execute(acceptWithBody(replaceIntent(prd.Body,'new intent'))); assert r.Terminate; assert contains(sink.get().Body,'new intent')

requirements.title: Rounds and stop reasons
requirements.rationale: Each round is two full phases, so the rounds stop as soon as nothing serious is found or the limit is reached.

criteria.condition: a review raises no findings
criteria.action: stop the rounds, record the round with an empty finding list and count it in `rounds_run`, and pass the PRD on unchanged
criteria.contract: `stop_reason` is `no_findings`

setup: the real round loop with a scripted reviewer that submits no findings and a reviser that fails the test if called
round limit 3
check.pseudocode: out, rv = runRounds(prd, limit=3); assert reviserCalls == 0 && out == prd; assert rv.RoundsRun == 1 && len(rv.Rounds[0].Findings) == 0; assert rv.StopReason == 'no_findings'

criteria.condition: a review raises one or more findings
criteria.action: run the revision phase of the same round on those findings
criteria.contract: the revision of round 1 ran on round 1's findings; the round-2 review was sent the body the revision produced; rounds_run is 2

setup: a scripted reviewer returning a major finding in round 1 and no findings in round 2
a scripted reviser that changes the body
round limit 2
check.pseudocode: out, rv = runRounds(prd, limit=2); assert reviserCalls == 1; assert reviewerReqs[1].PRD.Body == revisedBody; assert rv.RoundsRun == 2

criteria.condition: a round's revision finishes and that round's review raised at least one `critical` or `major` finding and fewer rounds than the round limit have run
criteria.action: start another round whose review reads the PRD as that revision left it

criteria.condition: a round's revision finishes and that round's review raised only `minor` findings
criteria.action: stop the rounds
criteria.contract: `stop_reason` is `no_serious_findings`

setup: a scripted reviewer returning only minor findings in round 1
round limit 5
check.pseudocode: out, rv = runRounds(prd, limit=5); assert reviserCalls == 1 && reviewerCalls == 1; assert rv.StopReason == 'no_serious_findings'

criteria.condition: a round's revision finishes and that round's review raised at least one `critical` or `major` finding and the number of rounds run equals the round limit
criteria.action: stop the rounds
criteria.contract: `stop_reason` is `rounds_exhausted`

setup: a scripted reviewer returning a critical finding every round
a reviser that finishes each time
round limit 2
check.pseudocode: out, rv = runRounds(prd, limit=2); assert reviewerCalls == 2 && reviserCalls == 2; assert rv.StopReason == 'rounds_exhausted'

criteria.condition: a round after the first starts
criteria.action: send both its reviewer and its reviser every earlier round's findings with their ids, dispositions and reasons, and tell the reviewer that it may raise a rejected finding again only with evidence the rejection did not answer and only by naming it in `reopens`
criteria.contract: both prompts contain R1-F1, R1-F2, their dispositions and 'REASON-Q'; the reviewer prompt says a rejected finding may be raised again only with evidence the rejection did not answer and only by naming it in `reopens`; the round-1 prompts contain no earlier-findings section

setup: round 1 findings R1-F1 (accepted) and R1-F2 (rejected with reason 'REASON-Q')
round limit 2 and a major finding in round 1
check.pseudocode: for p in [reviewerReqs[1], reviserReqs[1]]: assert contains(p,'R1-F2') && contains(p,'rejected') && contains(p,'REASON-Q'); assert contains(reviewerReqs[1],'reopens'); assert !contains(reviewerReqs[0],'R1-F')

criteria.action: for any round limit from 1 to 5 and any sequence of review and revision outcomes, run at most the round limit of reviews, end with exactly one `stop_reason`, and report `incomplete` whenever a review or revision did not finish or the budget stopped the rounds, ahead of every other reason
criteria.contract: the number of reviews is at most the round limit; stop_reason is exactly one of no_findings, no_serious_findings, rounds_exhausted, incomplete; stop_reason is incomplete whenever any phase failed or the budget stopped the rounds; otherwise stop_reason follows the last review and its revision

setup: a round loop driven by scripted reviewer and reviser outcomes (findings of any severity mix, empty, failure, budget stop)
check.pseudocode: for limit in 1..5, seq in gen_outcomes(): out, rv = runRounds(prd, limit, seq); assert reviews <= limit; assert rv.StopReason in set; if anyFailure(seq, used) then assert rv.StopReason == 'incomplete'

requirements.title: A round that cannot finish
requirements.rationale: The review only improves a PRD that is already complete, so losing the package because the critic failed would be worse than skipping the rest of the review.

criteria.condition: a review or revision phase ends without an accepted submission because of its budget, its turn limit, `--phase-timeout` while the run's context is still live, a refusal, or a model, API or internal error
criteria.action: stop the rounds, generate the package from the last complete PRD, and record a `high` warning `prd_review_incomplete` with stage `prd_review` that names the scope's spec name, the round, the failed phase (`prd_review` or `prd_revision`) and the reason it failed
criteria.contract: `stop_reason` is `incomplete`; the run's status and exit code are those it would have without the failure

setup: the real pipeline and rounds with a reviewer or reviser that fails by turn limit, timeout with a live context, refusal, API error and internal error in turn
the package otherwise generates
check.pseudocode: for fail in [turns,timeout,refusal,api,internal]: res = Run(opts, reviewerFails(fail)); w = warning(res,'prd_review_incomplete'); assert w.Severity=='high' && w.Stage=='prd_review'; assert contains(w.Message, specName) && contains(w.Message,'round 1') && contains(w.Message,'prd_review'); assert res.exit == 0

criteria.condition: a round's review finished but its revision did not finish
criteria.action: report that round's findings with the disposition `unanswered` and generate the package from the PRD the review read
criteria.contract: each such finding has `disposition` `unanswered` and no `reason`, and counts in `unanswered_count`

setup: a reviewer that submits two findings and a reviser that fails
check.pseudocode: out, rv = runRounds(prd, limit=2, reviserFails); for f in rv.Rounds[0].Findings: assert f.Disposition=='unanswered' && f.Reason==''; assert rv.UnansweredCount == 2; assert out == prd

criteria.condition: a review or revision is about to start and `--total-budget` is set and the run's spend so far has reached the total budget
criteria.action: not start the phase, stop the rounds as for a failed phase, and name the total budget, the spend and the ceiling as the reason in the `prd_review_incomplete` warning
criteria.contract: `stop_reason` is `incomplete`; `rounds_run` is 0 when the stop came before the first review; the exit code is unchanged

setup: --total-budget set and the run's recorded spend already at or above it
a reviewer fake that fails the test if called
check.pseudocode: run.AddPhase(costly); out, rv = runRounds(prd, totalBudget=run.CostUSD()); assert reviewerCalls==0 && rv.RoundsRun==0 && rv.StopReason=='incomplete'; assert contains(warn.Message,'total budget') && contains(warn.Message, spendStr) && contains(warn.Message, ceilingStr)

criteria.condition: the budget stops the rounds between a review and its revision
criteria.action: report that review's findings with the disposition `unanswered`
criteria.contract: each such finding counts in `unanswered_count`

setup: a review whose recorded cost pushes the spend to the total budget
a reviser fake that fails the test if called
check.pseudocode: out, rv = runRounds(prd, totalBudget=reviewCost); assert reviserCalls==0; assert all(f.Disposition=='unanswered' for f in rv.Rounds[0].Findings); assert rv.UnansweredCount == rv.FindingsCount

criteria.condition: the run's context is cancelled by Ctrl-C or SIGTERM during a review or revision
criteria.action: stop the run as an interrupted run, record no `prd_review_incomplete` warning, and generate no package from the interrupted PRD
criteria.contract: a failure with stage `prd_review` or `prd_revision`, category `aborted`, exit code 1

setup: a reviewer then a reviser fake that cancel the run's context while running
check.pseudocode: for ph in ['prd_review','prd_revision']: err = Run(ctx, opts with cancelDuring(ph)); f = asFailure(err); assert f.Stage==ph && f.Category=='aborted'; assert exitCode(err)==1; assert noWarning('prd_review_incomplete'); assert noPackage()

criteria.action: keep the existing total-budget check before each split scope's PRD phase after the first, failing the run with stage `budget` when the spend has reached the ceiling
criteria.contract: the run fails with stage `budget` and category budget; scope 2's PRD phase did not run

setup: a split of three scopes with --total-budget already reached after scope 1
check.pseudocode: err = Run(opts{TotalBudgetUSD: x}); f = asFailure(err); assert f.Stage=='budget' && f.Category==CategoryBudget; assert prdCalls == 1

requirements.title: Where the rounds run
requirements.rationale: Every PRD the run writes is reviewed before its package is reserved, and the next scope builds on the revised PRD rather than the original.

criteria.condition: the PRD of an undivided input has been written and any `--name` has been applied, while `--adversarial` is on
criteria.action: run the PRD's rounds before its package number is reserved and before its package is generated
criteria.contract: the review sees spec name 'custom_name'; the log order is prd, prd_review, prd_revision, reservePackage, requirements

setup: the real pipeline with an event log across author, reviewer, reviser, reservePackage and generation
--name 'custom_name' and --adversarial
check.pseudocode: assert order(log) == ['prd','prd_review','prd_revision','reserve','requirements']; assert reviewerReqs[0].PRD.SpecName == 'custom_name'

criteria.condition: a split scope's PRD phase has finished and the planned name has replaced any name the model chose, while `--adversarial` is on
criteria.action: run that PRD's rounds in the coordinator before the scope's package number is reserved and its package goroutine is started
criteria.contract: the review of scope 2 sees the planned name; scope 2's rounds finish before its reservePackage and before its package goroutine starts

setup: a two-scope split whose model-chosen name differs from the planned name
check.pseudocode: assert reviewerReqsFor(2).PRD.SpecName == plan[1].Name; assert idx(log,'rounds-done 2') < idx(log,'reserve 2') < idx(log,'build-start 2')

criteria.condition: the first scope of a split is reviewed
criteria.action: run its rounds after the split plan is recorded, inside the split loop, with a split context built for scope 1 like every other scope's
criteria.contract: the split plan file exists on disk before scope 1's review starts; scope 1's review request carries a splitContext with Index 0 and the full plan

setup: a split run where the PRD phase recommends a split
check.pseudocode: assert planSavedAt < firstReviewAt; assert reviewerReqs[0].Split != nil && reviewerReqs[0].Split.Index == 0 && len(reviewerReqs[0].Split.Plan.Scopes) == n

criteria.condition: the PRD phase of a split scope after the first starts
criteria.action: show it the earlier scopes' final PRDs and final `codebase_notes` as the rounds left them, not the PRD phase's originals
criteria.contract: its splitContext Drafts[0] has body 'REVISED-1'; its Notes[0] is 'NOTES-REV'; neither the original body nor the original notes appear

setup: scope 1's revision changed the body to 'REVISED-1' and the notes to 'NOTES-REV'
check.pseudocode: req = authorReqs[1]; assert req.Split.Drafts[0].Body == 'REVISED-1' && req.Split.Notes[0] == 'NOTES-REV'

criteria.condition: a split is resumed with `--adversarial`
criteria.action: review only the PRDs of the scopes written in this run and leave the packages written in earlier runs unreviewed
criteria.contract: the reviewer ran only for scopes 2 and 3; scope 1's package on disk is untouched and has no review round

setup: a split plan on disk with scope 1 already written and scopes 2 and 3 pending
check.pseudocode: Run(resumeOpts); assert reviewedScopes == ['scope2','scope3']; assert fileHash(scope1Dir) == before

requirements.title: The review in the result
requirements.rationale: A caller must see how each PRD was reviewed and what changed, while the package on disk keeps exactly the files the format defines.

criteria.condition: `--adversarial` is on
criteria.action: attach a `review` to the first package and to every package in `follow_on_specs`, including a package reported unwritten, with the fields `rounds_run`, `rounds_allowed`, `stop_reason`, `findings_count`, `accepted_count`, `rejected_count`, `unanswered_count` and `rounds`
criteria.contract: each `rounds` entry has its round number and its findings

setup: a three-scope split with --adversarial where the third scope's generation fails
check.pseudocode: assert res.Review != nil; for p in res.FollowOnSpecs: assert p.Review != nil; assert res.FollowOnSpecs[1].Written == false && res.FollowOnSpecs[1].Review != nil; assert res.Review.Rounds[0].Round == 1

criteria.action: report each finding with `id`, `severity`, `section`, `flaw`, `evidence`, `remedy`, `disposition`, `reopens` only when it is non-empty, and `reason` only when the disposition is `rejected`
criteria.contract: every finding has id, severity, section, flaw, evidence, remedy and disposition; reopens is present only on the finding that has one; reason is present only on the rejected finding

setup: findings: accepted without reopens, rejected with reason and reopens, unanswered
check.pseudocode: a = json(acc); assert !has(a,'reopens') && !has(a,'reason'); r = json(rej); assert r.reason == 'why' && r.reopens == 'R1-F1'; u = json(unans); assert !has(u,'reason')

criteria.action: for any package `review`, report `findings_count` equal to the number of findings over all rounds and equal to the sum of `accepted_count`, `rejected_count` and `unanswered_count`, and `rounds_run` equal to the number of `rounds` entries
criteria.contract: findings_count equals the number of findings over all rounds; findings_count equals accepted_count plus rejected_count plus unanswered_count; rounds_run equals the number of rounds entries

setup: the review record built by the round loop
check.pseudocode: for rounds in gen_rounds(): rv = buildReview(rounds); assert rv.FindingsCount == sum(len(r.Findings)); assert rv.FindingsCount == rv.Accepted+rv.Rejected+rv.Unanswered; assert rv.RoundsRun == len(rv.Rounds)

criteria.action: use the final PRD for the written `prd.md`, the PRD posted by `--comment`, `result.open_questions` and `result.relevant_files`, and send its body, `relevant_files` and notes to the generation and architecture phases
criteria.contract: prd.md on disk has the revised body; the posted comment is built from the revised PRD; result.open_questions and result.relevant_files are the revised ones; requirements, test_spec, tasks and architecture phases are sent the revised body, relevant files and notes

setup: a revision that changed the body, open questions, relevant files and notes
--comment enabled with a recording comment client
check.pseudocode: assert read(prdmd).contains(revBody); assert comment.contains(revBody); assert res.OpenQuestions == rev.OQ && res.RelevantFiles == rev.RF; for ph in genPhases: assert contains(ph.User, revBody) && contains(ph.User, rev.Notes)

criteria.action: write no review data into any package directory or into the `--comment` text, so that the package holds only the files the format defines
criteria.contract: the package directory holds only prd.md, requirements.json, test_spec.json, tasks.json (and architecture.md when asked); no file contains 'FINDING-MARK'; the posted comment does not contain it or a review section

setup: a run with findings whose text contains a unique marker 'FINDING-MARK'
check.pseudocode: assert sorted(ls(pkg)) == formatFiles; for f in ls(pkg): assert !contains(read(f),'FINDING-MARK'); assert !contains(comment,'FINDING-MARK')

criteria.condition: any package of the run carries a `review`
criteria.action: add after the open-questions clause the clause `review: <R> round(s), <F> finding(s), <A> accepted`, totalled over every package of the run, using the singular noun when a count is 1 and leaving out `, <A> accepted` when F is 0, inside the existing 200-character cap and before the high-warning clause
criteria.contract: for example `spec: wrote .specs/07_widget_cache; 2 open questions; review: 2 rounds, 9 findings, 7 accepted`

setup: results whose packages carry reviews: 2 rounds/9 findings/7 accepted; 1 round/1 finding/1 accepted; 1 round/0 findings; a long-named result near the 200-character cap; a result with a high warning
check.pseudocode: assert Summary(r1) == 'spec: wrote .specs/07_widget_cache; 2 open questions; review: 2 rounds, 9 findings, 7 accepted'; assert contains(Summary(r2),'review: 1 round, 1 finding, 1 accepted'); assert endsWith(Summary(r3),'review: 1 round, 0 findings'); assert runeLen(envSummary(rLong)) <= 200

criteria.condition: the result is emitted with `--detail summary`
criteria.action: keep the first package's `review` with every field except `rounds`, so the result still decodes into `envelope.SpecResult`
criteria.contract: the review keeps rounds_run, rounds_allowed, stop_reason and the four counts; the review has no rounds field; the JSON decodes into envelope.SpecResult without error and with the counts intact

setup: a Result whose first package has a review with two rounds
check.pseudocode: v = res.SummaryView(); b = json(v); assert has(b,'review.stop_reason') && !has(b,'review.rounds'); var sr envelope.SpecResult; assert json.Unmarshal(b,&sr)==nil; assert sr.Review.FindingsCount == n

requirements.title: Progress, usage, preflight and models
requirements.rationale: Review phases are phases like any other: they are shown, bounded, priced and resolved to a model the same way.

criteria.condition: a review or revision phase runs
criteria.action: report it on stderr through the same begin and done lines and turns-and-tokens footer as every other phase, labelled `reviewing the PRD (round r of L)` or `revising the PRD (round r of L)` with the scope prefix in a split, then print a line with the number of findings by severity after a review, or the number accepted and rejected after a revision
criteria.contract: for example `scope 2 of 3 (issuex_github): reviewing the PRD (round 1 of 2)`

setup: a split run of three scopes with --adversarial-rounds 2 and a progress writer capturing stderr
scope 2 review raises one critical and two minor findings, its revision accepts two and rejects one
check.pseudocode: out = stderr(); assert contains(out,'scope 2 of 3 (issuex_github): reviewing the PRD (round 1 of 2)'); assert contains(out,'revising the PRD (round 1 of 2)'); assert regex(out,'1 critical.*2 minor'); assert regex(out,'2 accepted.*1 rejected')

criteria.condition: a review or revision phase ends
criteria.action: record it in `usage.phases[]` under the name `prd_review` or `prd_revision` with its scope, model, effort, turns and cost, and count its cost in the run's spend
criteria.contract: usage.phases contains entries named `prd_review` and `prd_revision` with scope, model, effort, turns and cost; Run.CostUSD includes their cost

setup: a run with scripted review and revision phases that each report a model, effort, turns and cost
check.pseudocode: p = usagePhases(env); assert has(p,'prd_review') && has(p,'prd_revision'); assert p['prd_review'].Model != '' && p['prd_review'].Turns > 0; assert run.CostUSD() == sum(cost of all phases)

criteria.condition: `--preflight` is given with `--adversarial`
criteria.action: set `estimate.phases` to (1 + 3, plus 1 with `--architecture`, + 2 × round limit) × packages, derive `max_total_usd` from it, and list `prd_review` and `prd_revision` with their model and effort after `prd` in the `phase_models` check detail
criteria.contract: estimate.phases is 1 + 3 + 2×3 = 10 (11 with --architecture) times the package count; max_total_usd equals phases times the per-phase ceiling; the phase_models detail lists prd_review and prd_revision with model and effort immediately after prd

setup: a preflight run for a fresh input of one package with rounds 3, with and without --architecture
check.pseudocode: r = RunPreflight(opts{Adversarial:true, Rounds:3}); assert r.Estimate.Phases == 10*pkgs; assert r.Estimate.MaxTotalUSD == r.Estimate.Phases*MaxBudgetPerPhaseUSD; d = detail(r,'phase_models'); assert idx(d,'prd_review') == idx(d,'prd')+1 && idx(d,'prd_revision') == idx(d,'prd_review')+1

criteria.condition: `--preflight` is given without `--adversarial`
criteria.action: produce the same `estimate.phases`, `max_total_usd` and `phase_models` detail as before this feature
criteria.contract: estimate.phases is (1+3[+1])×packages; phase_models detail lists prd, requirements, test_spec, tasks (architecture only with the flag) and neither prd_review nor prd_revision

setup: a preflight run without --adversarial, with and without --architecture
check.pseudocode: r = RunPreflight(opts{}); assert r.Estimate.Phases == 4*pkgs; d = detail(r,'phase_models'); assert !contains(d,'prd_review') && !contains(d,'prd_revision')

criteria.action: accept `prd_review` and `prd_revision` in `--phase-model` and resolve both, when no choice names them, to `claude-sonnet-5-5` `medium` on SIMPLE, `claude-sonnet-5-5` `high` on STANDARD and `claude-opus-5-5` `xhigh` on ADVANCED
criteria.contract: both choices parse without error; SIMPLE resolves both to claude-sonnet-5-5 medium; STANDARD resolves both to claude-sonnet-5-5 high; ADVANCED resolves both to claude-opus-5-5 xhigh

setup: tiers SIMPLE, STANDARD and ADVANCED with no phase choice naming the new phases
check.pseudocode: assert ParsePhaseChoice('prd_review=claude-opus-5-5') ok; for (tier,m,e) in table: p = ResolvePlan(tier); assert p.Phases['prd_review'] == (m,e) && p.Phases['prd_revision'] == (m,e)

criteria.action: apply a model id given to `--model` and `--effort` or `$AF_MODEL_EFFORT` to `prd_review` and `prd_revision`, leave them unmoved by `--phase-model prd=…`, and bound each review and revision by `--budget`, `--max-turns`, `--phase-timeout` and `--max-tokens` as a phase of its own
criteria.contract: `model.phases` shows the `--model` id and effort for `prd_review` and `prd_revision`; a review that exceeds `--budget`, `--max-turns`, `--phase-timeout` or `--max-tokens` stops on its own bound

setup: a plan resolved with --model X, --effort high, and a separate plan with `--phase-model prd=claude-opus-5-5`
the real Runner with a fake model, bounds of a small --max-turns, --budget, --phase-timeout and --max-tokens in turn
a PRD phase that stayed within the bounds
check.pseudocode:
p = ResolvePlan(model:'X', effort:'high'); assert p['prd_review'].Model=='X' && p['prd_revision'].Effort=='high'; q = ResolvePlan(choices:['prd=claude-opus-5-5']); assert q['prd'].Model=='claude-opus-5-5' && q['prd_review'] == tierBase
for bound in [turns,budget,timeout]: _, res, err = reviewer.Review(ctx, req); assert err != nil && res.StopReason == bound; assert recordedPhase.MaxTokens == maxTokens

criteria.action: list `prd_review` and `prd_revision` in `model.phases`, the `--phase-model` help and the `effort_clamped` warning whether or not `--adversarial` is on
criteria.contract: model.phases includes prd_review and prd_revision; the --phase-model usage string names both; the effort_clamped warning lists both phases when clamping applies

setup: spec runs without --adversarial, one with an effort the model clamps
check.pseudocode: env = run(args); assert has(env.Model.Phases,'prd_review') && has(env.Model.Phases,'prd_revision'); assert contains(helpText,'prd_review') && contains(helpText,'prd_revision'); assert contains(clampWarning.Message,'prd_review')

execution_paths.title: An undivided input is reviewed, revised and generated from the revised PRD

steps.action: runs `spec --adversarial --adversarial-rounds 2` on an input
validates the flags and starts the specgen pipeline with a round limit of 2
runs the PRD phase and writes the first PRD
submits findings including a `major` one, which the run numbers `R1-F1` onwards
answers every finding and submits the revised body
reviews the revised PRD in round 2 and submits no findings
reserves the package, generates requirements, test spec and tasks from the final PRD and writes `prd.md` from it
emits a result whose package carries `review` with `stop_reason` `no_findings`, and a summary with the review clause, exit 0

setup: the spec command with a scripted provider: PRD phase, round-1 review with a major finding, round-1 revision that changes the body, round-2 review with no findings, then generation phases
the valid_spec fixture and an empty specs dir
end_state: exit code 0
phases ran in order prd, prd_review, prd_revision, prd_review, requirements, test_spec, tasks
finding ids start at R1-F1
the written prd.md has the revised body and the package validates
the package carries a review with rounds_run 2, rounds_allowed 2 and stop_reason `no_findings`
the summary contains `review: 2 rounds, 1 finding, 1 accepted`
smoke.pseudocode: r = runSpecCmd(['--adversarial','--adversarial-rounds','2', input]); assert r.exit==0; assert phases(r)==[...]; assert read(prdmd)==revisedBody; assert r.pkg.Review.StopReason=='no_findings'; assert contains(r.env.summary,'review: 2 rounds')

execution_paths.title: Each split scope is reviewed in the coordinator before its package starts

steps.action: runs `spec --adversarial` on an input the PRD phase splits into scopes
records the split plan, then runs scope 1's rounds with its split context
reserves scope 1's package and starts its generation goroutine with the final PRD
runs scope 2's PRD phase, showing it scope 1's revised PRD and notes, then runs scope 2's rounds
writes every scope's package from its final PRD
emits a result in which the first package and every `follow_on_specs` package carry `review`, and a summary clause totalled over all packages

setup: a scripted provider whose PRD phase recommends a three-scope split, with reviews and revisions for each scope
a real specs dir
end_state: the split plan is recorded before scope 1's review
scope 2's PRD phase is shown scope 1's revised PRD and notes
every package is written from its final PRD
the first package and every follow_on_specs package carry a review
the summary clause totals rounds, findings and accepted over all packages
exit code 0
smoke.pseudocode: r = runSpecCmd(['--adversarial', input]); assert planSavedBeforeFirstReview; assert authorReq[1].Drafts[0].Body == revised1; for p in allPackages(r): assert p.Review != nil; assert summaryTotals(r) == sum(p.Review)

execution_paths.title: A review that cannot finish leaves a warning and the package from the last complete PRD

steps.action: runs `spec --adversarial` with a per-phase `--budget` too small for the review phase
runs the PRD phase and starts round 1's review
stops at its budget without an accepted submission
stops the rounds and records a `high` `prd_review_incomplete` warning naming the scope, round 1, `prd_review` and the reason
generates and writes the package from the PRD phase's PRD
emits a result whose `review` has `stop_reason` `incomplete`, with the exit code of a run without the failure

setup: the spec command with a per-phase --budget the scripted review phase exceeds before submitting
scripted PRD and generation phases
end_state: exit code is 0, as for a run without the failure
a high prd_review_incomplete warning names the spec name, round 1, prd_review and the budget reason
the package on disk is generated from the PRD phase's PRD
the review has stop_reason `incomplete`
smoke.pseudocode: r = runSpecCmd(['--adversarial','--budget',small,input]); assert r.exit==0; w = warning(r,'prd_review_incomplete'); assert w.Severity=='high'; assert read(prdmd)==originalBody; assert r.pkg.Review.StopReason=='incomplete'

steps.action: runs `spec --preflight --adversarial --adversarial-rounds 3`
computes `estimate.phases` as (1 + 3 + 2 × 3) × packages and `max_total_usd` from it
lists `prd_review` and `prd_revision` with model and effort after `prd` in the `phase_models` check
emits the preflight result without calling any model

setup: the spec command with a provider that fails the test if a model is called
end_state: exit code 0 and no model was called
estimate.phases is (1 + 3 + 2×3) × packages
max_total_usd derives from that count
the phase_models check lists prd_review and prd_revision with model and effort after prd
smoke.pseudocode: r = runSpecCmd(['--preflight','--adversarial','--adversarial-rounds','3', input]); assert r.exit==0 && modelCalls==0; assert r.env.estimate.phases == 10*pkgs; assert order(detail,'prd','prd_review','prd_revision')
